metadata.methods_description: EEG was recorded with an EMOTIV EPOC X headset (14 EEG channels, 128 Hz, hardware bandpass only) alongside continuously logged contact-quality and EEG-quality signals. All participants completed four conditions in a fixed order: eyes-open, eyes-closed, jungle soundscape, deconstruct soundscape. Liking ratings were collected for the soundscapes. Data are stored as EDF files with event markers for each segment.

citation_details.title: EEG and hedonic responses to sonic-seasoning soundscapes: a dataset
citation_details.author: Attila Pohlmann, Felipe Reinoso‐Carvalho, Brayan Rodríguez
citation_details.abstract: This dataset comprises electroencephalographic (EEG) recordings from 30 adult participants exposed to two contrasting designed soundscapes - a natural, sustainability-conveying "organic jungle" soundscape and a contrasting "deconstruct" soundscape - together with their liking ratings of each soundscape and basic demographic information. The data extend the largely behavioral "sonic-seasoning" literature, which has shown that sound and music systematically shape the sensory and affective evaluation of consumer experiences, by adding a complementary neurophysiological measurement angle. EEG was acquired with a 14-channel consumer-grade EMOTIV EPOC X headset (128 Hz) on a web-based experiment platform that logged synchronized event markers. For each participant the dataset provides: a resting calibration recording (eyes-open and eyes-closed); the EEG recorded during a brief (∼17 s) isolated exposure to each of the two soundscapes; the corresponding liking ratings; the soundscape stimulus
